items.explanation: Two overlapping current oral anticoagulant prescriptions: apixaban 5 mg twice daily and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily, both ordered 7/15/2026 with dispense validity running past the 9/24/2026 evaluation date. The 7/15/2026 cardiology note documents a switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starts apixaban, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped, so the patient is on two DOACs simultaneously.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 6/17/2026 to 1/6/2027). Most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm about 59 bpm with QT 564 ms and RR 1.01 s, Bazett QTc about 561 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 6/17/2026) are acceptable. Also on metoprolol succinate; marked QTc prolongation on amiodarone in a 95-year-old requires prescriber review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start is on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was obtained 3/7/2026, five days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo window of 30 days applies: ECG due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025, when it first appears in the current medication list. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo window of 30 days applies: ECG due by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was obtained 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 543 ms - see the separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026; it is absent from the 2/18/2026 medication list and present from 8/1/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. The only ECG on file (106035722) is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was first ordered at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so the revised 14-day window applies and an ECG was due by 4/24/2026. The only ECG (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - inside the superseded 30-day window but outside the 14-day requirement - so the requirement was not met in time and remains overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracing 3/9/2025), but the due date falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation time, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026; start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG exists in the chart for this patient, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - with the report requested by fax and not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined from the chart.

Cardiology clinic clinician note of 9/1/2026 documents a warfarin dose change (INR 1.6 subtherapeutic, increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily, recheck INR). Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR(PT) 2.3 was drawn 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

Anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 documents a warfarin dose change made under the clinic protocol (home INR 3.4; warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily), which the 6/1/2024 standing order permits pharmacists to make. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR(PT) in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, and the reported home INR was the pre-change value. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 10:55 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72." Both ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at about 140-145 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, contradicting the documented sinus rhythm at rate 72.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current prescription (ordered 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027) despite outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 documenting admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The clinic reissued apixaban without documenting that review; concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel further increase bleeding risk. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, combined systolic/diastolic CHF), hypertension, age 80 (2), diabetes mellitus type 2, prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual deficits (2), vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis), female sex. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only; no oral anticoagulant is prescribed. Guideline-recommended (Class 1) anticoagulation is absent - antiplatelet therapy alone is not an acceptable substitute.

71-year-old woman with charted paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0). CHA2DS2-VASc 5: hypertension, age 71 (65-74), prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia/hemiparesis (2 points), female sex. Current medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate; no anticoagulant is prescribed at any clinic visit through 6/23/2026. Rate control only, without guideline-recommended (Class 1) oral anticoagulation, in a patient with prior stroke.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation charted as a condition and carried in the history of every cardiology clinic note (10/10/2025 to 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3: hypertension, age 71 (65-74), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). Only current medication is levothyroxine 50 mcg daily; no oral anticoagulant and no antiplatelet. Score of 3 in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of any anticoagulant needs review (past procedural haemorrhage is noted in the history and should be weighed).

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 7/18/2026 to 12/26/2026). Most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm 68 bpm with QT 492 ms and RR 0.88 s, giving a Bazett QTc of about 525 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Latest electrolytes 3/18/2026: potassium 3.8 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both low-normal). Note of 5/14/2024 recorded this ECG as having an acceptable QT, which the measured interval does not support.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 7/15/2026 to 1/7/2027; 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg maximum usually advised on QT grounds). Most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm 70 bpm with QT 487 ms and RR 0.86 s, Bazett QTc about 526 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 7/12/2026 to 1/9/2027, started at the 11/10/2025 cardiology clinic visit). Most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm 62 bpm with QT 534 ms and RR 0.97 s, Bazett QTc about 543 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 6/9/2026) are normal. QTc rose from 438 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing after amiodarone was started.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with mild variability; upright P in II/aVF, one P per QRS, PR 122 ms. Narrow QRS 80 ms with normal precordial progression, frontal axis about +48 degrees. QT 324 ms at RR 0.74 s gives QTc 376 ms. No conduction block. No prior tracing for comparison. Confirms the 3/7/2026 note documenting sinus rhythm and satisfies the post-citalopram ECG requirement.

Sinus tachycardia 104 bpm, regular, discrete upright P in II with PR about 130 ms. QRS 94 ms, axis about +40 degrees, tall upright T in V2-V3. QT 337 ms at RR 0.58 s, QTc 443 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG 6/20/2025 was sinus tachycardia 147 bpm with PR about 125 ms and QTc about 400-420 ms; rate has slowed, with no new arrhythmia and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus tachycardia about 109 bpm, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II and PR about 120 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis about +36 degrees. QT 330 ms at RR 0.55 s, QTc (Bazett) 445 ms - upper normal. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG on file, so no comparison available.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean ventricular rate about 136 bpm (peak instantaneous rate near 170). RR intervals vary chaotically from 0.35 to 0.65 s with no consistent atrial activity preceding the QRS complexes, so PR is not measurable. QRS 100 ms, frontal axis near 0 degrees. QT 296 ms at mean RR 0.44 s, QTc (Bazett) about 458 ms (rate-correction unreliable at this rate). The tracing 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094) was also atrial fibrillation at about 134-142 bpm with QTc 453 ms, so there is no change between the two. Both contradict the same-day note of sinus rhythm at 72 bpm.

Regular supraventricular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s) with consistent low-amplitude atrial deflections about 150 ms before each QRS; P vector is leftward/superior (positive in I, low-amplitude negative in II/aVF), so a low atrial pacemaker cannot be excluded, but the rhythm is regular and one-to-one and is read as sinus. QRS 86 ms, tall R in I/aVL with net negative II/III, frontal axis about -25 degrees. QTc 431 ms. Prior ECG 4/27/2025 showed the same pattern at 60 bpm with QTc 404 ms - no new arrhythmia, block, or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular, with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 118 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +5 degrees. QT 292 ms at RR 0.62 s, QTc 373 ms. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG on file for this patient.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 0.83 s), upright P in II with PR about 140 ms. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +21 degrees. QT 373 ms, QTc (Bazett) 409 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG on file; it predates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

Atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate about 63 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.70, 0.74, 1.13, 1.15, 1.16 s; CV 0.21) with no organised P wave in any lead before the QRS complexes, so PR is not measurable. QRS 92 ms, frontal axis about +14 degrees. QT approximately 430 ms at mean RR 0.96 s, QTc (Bazett) about 440 ms. Prior ECG three days earlier (11/12/2024) was normal sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with PR 162 ms and QTc 396 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation; the QTc difference (about 45 ms) does not reach 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm/borderline sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with clear upright P waves in II (0.2 mV) and PR about 115 ms. QRS 88 ms, tall R in II/aVF, frontal axis about +62 degrees. QT 422 ms at RR 1.03 s, QTc 416 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG the previous day (3/8/2025) was sinus 62 bpm, QRS 88 ms, QTc 436 ms - no change. Baseline tracing predates the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, very regular (RR 0.72 s), upright P in II/aVF with PR about 142 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees. QT 342 ms, QTc (Bazett) 403 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 0.78 s), with prominent upright P waves in II/aVF (0.26 mV) and PR about 160-165 ms. Narrow QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +63 degrees. Broad symmetric T waves; QT approximately 405-430 ms at RR 0.78 s, giving QTc (Bazett) of roughly 470 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG 2/2/2020 was sinus 75 bpm with QTc about 495 ms, so the change is well under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s, CV 0.005), upright P waves in II with PR about 195 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 86 ms, axis about +49 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 388 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus 108 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QTc 411 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no bundle branch block and QTc change of only -23 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with prolonged AV conduction: P onset about 250 ms and QRS onset about 40 ms before the R peak, PR approximately 205-210 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 82 ms with dominant R in V4-V6, frontal axis about +12 degrees. QT 395 ms at RR 1.10 s, QTc (Bazett) 376 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 11/30/2024 was sinus 51 bpm with a single ectopic beat, PR about 180-185 ms and QTc 360 ms; no new arrhythmia, bundle branch block or 60 ms QTc shift.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean ventricular rate about 147 bpm. RR intervals range from 0.31 to 0.60 s with no repeatable atrial deflection before the QRS (P-window correlation 0.15), so PR is not measurable. QRS about 80 ms, frontal axis near -8 degrees. QT 261 ms at mean RR 0.41 s, QTc (Bazett) about 410 ms. The tracing 12 hours earlier (9/12/2025 18:57) was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with PR 144 ms and QTc 405 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation; intravenous amiodarone was started the same morning.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm with upright P waves in II (0.22 mV) and PR about 165 ms, confirming the same-day note of sinus rhythm. QRS 92 ms, frontal axis about +12 degrees. QT 355 ms at RR 0.82 s, QTc (Bazett) 392 ms. No conduction block. The prior tracing of 11/21/2025 was sinus 67 bpm with a markedly long QT (about 500 ms, QTc 529 ms); repolarisation has now normalised, a QTc decrease of well over 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm (RR 0.81 s) after two early supraventricular beats at the start of the recording; thereafter the rhythm is regular with consistent upright P waves in II and PR about 175 ms. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about +57 degrees. QT 382 ms, QTc (Bazett) 425 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, very regular (RR 0.538 s, CV 0.003), with a single upright P wave in II about 145 ms before each QRS - no flutter waves and no second atrial deflection per cycle, so the charted atrial flutter is not present on this tracing. QRS 96 ms with deep S in V1 and tall R in II, frontal axis about +35 degrees. QT 295 ms, QTc (Bazett) 402 ms. Prior ECG 7/4/2022 was virtually identical (sinus 115 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QTc 397 ms) - no change.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm interrupted by one early beat with a compensatory pause (RR 0.55 s then 1.36 s); otherwise regular at RR 0.98 s with broad low-amplitude P waves and PR about 195-200 ms (borderline, just short of first-degree block). QRS 104 ms, dominant R in I/aVL with net negative II, III and aVF, giving a left axis of about -30 to -35 degrees (left anterior fascicular pattern). QT 377 ms, QTc (Bazett) 381 ms. No bundle branch block. Single ECG on file - no atrial fibrillation captured despite the charted paroxysmal AF.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with one atrial deflection before every QRS at a constant interval of about 140 ms, read as sinus. The limb leads are globally inverted - QRS and P both negative in I, II and aVL and positive in aVR - while precordial progression is normal, giving a calculated frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme/north-west quadrant); left-right arm lead reversal should be excluded before accepting this axis as real. QRS 90 ms, QT 349 ms, QTc (Bazett) 376 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file; it postdates the 4/10/2026 escitalopram start by 19 days.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, PR about 122 ms, QRS 98 ms, frontal axis about +42 degrees. Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with a late broad T wave peaking near 370 ms and ending near 450 ms: QT 487 ms at RR 0.86 s, QTc (Bazett) 526 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 6/17/2020 was sinus tachycardia 132 bpm with QTc about 350 ms, so QTc has risen far more than 60 ms - relevant to citalopram 40 mg daily (see QT safety item).

Normal sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 0.88 s), upright P in II with PR about 118 ms. QRS 84 ms, frontal axis about +64 degrees. QT 407 ms, QTc (Bazett) 434 ms - within normal limits. No conduction block. Single ECG on file; obtained 3/8/2026, 24 days after escitalopram was started, satisfying the 30-day monitoring window then in force.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, regular (RR 1.14 s), upright P waves in II with PR about 165-170 ms. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about -6 degrees. QT 386 ms, QTc (Bazett) 363 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG 12/13/2018 was sinus 66 bpm with QRS 102 ms, PR about 195 ms and QTc 388 ms - no new arrhythmia, bundle branch block or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis about +45 degrees. Markedly prolonged repolarisation: T wave peaks near 370 ms and ends near 455 ms after the R wave, QT 492 ms at RR 0.88 s, QTc (Bazett) 525 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 11/23/2022 was sinus 74 bpm with QTc 362 ms, so QTc has increased by roughly 160 ms - relevant to ongoing escitalopram (see QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm. Despite the fast rate the rhythm is regular (RR 0.40-0.45 s, CV 0.02) and a small but reproducible atrial deflection precedes every QRS at a fixed interval of about 130 ms (beat-to-beat P correlation 0.98); there is a single atrial wave per cycle, with no sawtooth flutter activity. No pacing spikes are seen despite the charted pacemaker. QRS 76 ms with deep S in V1-V2, frontal axis about +2 degrees. QT 262 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 400 ms. Prior ECG 7/11/2022 was atrial fibrillation at about 110 bpm, so atrial fibrillation has resolved with restoration of an organised atrial rhythm.

Normal sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 0.73 s), upright P in II with P onset about 205 ms and QRS onset about 55 ms before the R peak, PR approximately 150 ms. QRS 102 ms - slightly broad but without a bundle branch block pattern (no rSR' in V1, no broad monophasic R in V6). Frontal axis about +32 degrees. QT 366 ms, QTc (Bazett) 428 ms. Single ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular, upright P in II with PR about 130 ms. Narrow QRS 78 ms, frontal axis about -18 degrees. QT 338 ms at RR 0.66 s, QTc (Bazett) 416 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG 5/16/2021 was sinus 87 bpm, QRS 82 ms, QTc 394 ms - no new arrhythmia, block, or 60 ms QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with first-degree AV block (P onset about 270 ms and QRS onset about 60 ms before the R peak, PR approximately 210 ms) and left bundle branch block: QRS 126 ms, broad notched monophasic R in I, aVL and V6 with no S wave, and deep wide QS complexes in V1-V3. Frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal quadrant). QT 439 ms at RR 0.98 s, QTc (Bazett) 443 ms. The prior tracing of 6/3/2024 showed the identical pattern (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 210 ms, LBBB with QRS 128 ms, QTc 449 ms), so nothing has changed.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, regular, upright P in II with PR about 136 ms. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about +45 degrees. QT 333 ms at RR 0.59 s, QTc (Bazett) 431 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG the previous day (3/18/2025) was essentially identical - sinus 102 bpm, QRS 88 ms, QTc 428 ms - so there are no changes.

Underlying sinus rhythm at 66 bpm (RR 0.91 s) with consistent upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 150 ms. There is one pause of 1.82 s, exactly twice the baseline cycle length, consistent with a single blocked/non-conducted sinus beat, plus two late short cycles (0.47, 0.46 s) from early supraventricular beats; overall the atrial rhythm is sinus and conducted PR intervals are normal. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about -21 degrees. QT 370 ms, QTc (Bazett) 388 ms. No bundle branch block. Only ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at about 59-60 bpm (RR 0.97-1.10 s) with reproducible upright P waves in II and PR about 175 ms, interrupted by one early beat with a compensatory pause. QRS 86 ms, frontal axis about +34 degrees. Repolarisation is grossly prolonged: broad T waves peaking near 420 ms and ending near 520 ms, QT 564 ms at RR 1.01 s, QTc (Bazett) 561 ms. No bundle branch block. The prior tracing of 4/6/2022 was atrial fibrillation at about 129 bpm with QTc 353 ms, so organised sinus rhythm has been restored (resolved AF) while QTc has increased by more than 200 ms on amiodarone.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, regular (RR 0.56 s, CV 0.005), with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 150 ms. Narrow QRS 66 ms, frontal axis about +50 degrees. QT 313 ms, QTc (Bazett) 418 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG 7/27/2019 was sinus 75 bpm with QRS 70 ms and QTc 417 ms - rate has risen but there is no new arrhythmia, bundle branch block or QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia 121 bpm, strikingly regular (RR 0.497 s). Upright P in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR about 150 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, tall R in V5/V6 with rS in V1-V2, frontal axis about +67 degrees. QT 280 ms at RR 0.50 s, QTc 397 ms. No conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, so no comparison possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, axis about +58 degrees, QT 325 ms at RR 0.59 s giving QTc 423 ms. No conduction block. The immediately preceding tracing (102910502, obtained 34 seconds earlier the same morning) was identical - sinus 100 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc 422 ms - so there are no interval or rhythm changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with low-amplitude but consistent P waves in II and PR about 168 ms; no dropped beats or Wenckebach on this 10-second sample despite the charted history of Mobitz II block. QRS 92 ms, axis about +35 degrees, QTc 401 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 was sinus 58 bpm with one ectopic beat, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms - no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia 122 bpm (RR 0.494 s, very regular), P waves upright in II with PR about 150 ms. QRS is now narrow at about 76 ms with low limb-lead voltage; net QRS is negative in I and positive in III/aVF, giving a rightward frontal axis (about +110 to +140 degrees). QTc roughly 418 ms. On the tracing 13 hours earlier (106516875, same day 01:33) QRS was 130-155 ms with an rSR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - typical right bundle branch block - which has now resolved, indicating intermittent RBBB. QTc essentially unchanged (about 420-465 ms then).

Sinus rhythm 62 bpm, PR about 170 ms, QRS 98 ms, prominent left-sided voltage (V5 R 2.7 mV), frontal axis about +65 degrees. Grossly prolonged repolarisation with T peak near 400 ms and T end near 485 ms: QT 534 ms at RR 0.97 s, QTc (Bazett) 543 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 was sinus bradycardia 53 bpm with QTc 438 ms, so QTc has increased by about 105 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 103 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.39-1.07 s, CV 0.28) with no reproducible P wave before any QRS (beat-to-beat P-window correlation only 0.38), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 80 ms; net QRS negative in II, III and aVF with positive I/aVL gives a left axis of about -58 degrees. QT 310 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 403 ms. Only ECG on file.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 6/17/2026 to 1/6/2027). Most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm about 59 bpm with QT 564 ms and RR 1.01 s, Bazett QTc about 561 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 6/17/2026) are acceptable. Also on metoprolol succinate; marked QTc prolongation on amiodarone in a 95-year-old requires prescriber review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start is on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was obtained 3/7/2026, five days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo window of 30 days applies: ECG due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025, when it first appears in the current medication list. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo window of 30 days applies: ECG due by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was obtained 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 543 ms - see the separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026; it is absent from the 2/18/2026 medication list and present from 8/1/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. The only ECG on file (106035722) is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was first ordered at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so the revised 14-day window applies and an ECG was due by 4/24/2026. The only ECG (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - inside the superseded 30-day window but outside the 14-day requirement - so the requirement was not met in time and remains overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracing 3/9/2025), but the due date falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation time, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026; start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG exists in the chart for this patient, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - with the report requested by fax and not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined from the chart.

Cardiology clinic clinician note of 9/1/2026 documents a warfarin dose change (INR 1.6 subtherapeutic, increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily, recheck INR). Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR(PT) 2.3 was drawn 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

Anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 documents a warfarin dose change made under the clinic protocol (home INR 3.4; warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily), which the 6/1/2024 standing order permits pharmacists to make. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR(PT) in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, and the reported home INR was the pre-change value. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 10:55 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72." Both ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at about 140-145 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, contradicting the documented sinus rhythm at rate 72.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current prescription (ordered 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027) despite outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 documenting admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The clinic reissued apixaban without documenting that review; concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel further increase bleeding risk. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, combined systolic/diastolic CHF), hypertension, age 80 (2), diabetes mellitus type 2, prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual deficits (2), vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis), female sex. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only; no oral anticoagulant is prescribed. Guideline-recommended (Class 1) anticoagulation is absent - antiplatelet therapy alone is not an acceptable substitute.

71-year-old woman with charted paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0). CHA2DS2-VASc 5: hypertension, age 71 (65-74), prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia/hemiparesis (2 points), female sex. Current medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate; no anticoagulant is prescribed at any clinic visit through 6/23/2026. Rate control only, without guideline-recommended (Class 1) oral anticoagulation, in a patient with prior stroke.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation charted as a condition and carried in the history of every cardiology clinic note (10/10/2025 to 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3: hypertension, age 71 (65-74), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). Only current medication is levothyroxine 50 mcg daily; no oral anticoagulant and no antiplatelet. Score of 3 in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of any anticoagulant needs review (past procedural haemorrhage is noted in the history and should be weighed).

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 7/18/2026 to 12/26/2026). Most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm 68 bpm with QT 492 ms and RR 0.88 s, giving a Bazett QTc of about 525 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Latest electrolytes 3/18/2026: potassium 3.8 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both low-normal). Note of 5/14/2024 recorded this ECG as having an acceptable QT, which the measured interval does not support.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 7/15/2026 to 1/7/2027; 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg maximum usually advised on QT grounds). Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes.

arguments.explanation: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean ventricular rate about 147 bpm. RR intervals range from 0.31 to 0.60 s with no repeatable atrial deflection before the QRS (P-window correlation 0.15), so PR is not measurable. QRS about 80 ms, frontal axis near -8 degrees. QT 261 ms at mean RR 0.41 s, QTc (Bazett) about 410 ms. The tracing 12 hours earlier (9/12/2025 18:57) was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with PR 144 ms and QTc 405 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation; intravenous amiodarone was started the same morning.

Guideline-recommended (Class 1) anticoagulation is absent - antiplatelet therapy alone is not an acceptable substitute.

Confirms the 3/7/2026 note documenting sinus rhythm and satisfies the post-citalopram ECG requirement.

Prior ECG 6/20/2025 was sinus tachycardia 147 bpm with PR about 125 ms and QTc about 400-420 ms; rate has slowed, with no new arrhythmia and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus tachycardia about 109 bpm, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II and PR about 120 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis about +36 degrees. QT 330 ms at RR 0.55 s, QTc (Bazett) 445 ms - upper normal. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG on file, so no comparison available.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s, CV 0.005), upright P waves in II with PR about 195 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 86 ms, axis about +49 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 388 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus 108 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QTc 411 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no bundle branch block and QTc change of only -23 ms.

Sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis about +45 degrees. Prior ECG 11/23/2022 was sinus 74 bpm with QTc 362 ms, so QTc has increased by roughly 160 ms - relevant to ongoing escitalopram (see QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia 121 bpm, strikingly regular (RR 0.497 s). Upright P in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR about 150 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, tall R in V5/V6 with rS in V1-V2, frontal axis about +67 degrees. QT 280 ms at RR 0.50 s, QTc 397 ms. No conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, so no comparison possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, axis about +58 degrees, QT 325 ms at RR 0.59 s giving QTc 423 ms. No conduction block. The immediately preceding tracing (102910502, obtained 34 seconds earlier the same morning) was identical - sinus 100 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc 422 ms - so there are no interval or rhythm changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with low-amplitude but consistent P waves in II and PR about 168 ms; no dropped beats or Wenckebach on this 10-second sample despite the charted history of Mobitz II block. QRS 92 ms, axis about +35 degrees, QTc 401 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 was sinus 58 bpm with one ectopic beat, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms - no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia 122 bpm (RR 0.494 s, very regular), P waves upright in II with PR about 150 ms. QRS is now narrow at about 76 ms with low limb-lead voltage; net QRS is negative in I and positive in III/aVF, giving a rightward frontal axis (about +110 to +140 degrees). QTc roughly 418 ms. On the tracing 13 hours earlier (106516875, same day 01:33) QRS was 130-155 ms with an rSR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - typical right bundle branch block - which has now resolved, indicating intermittent RBBB. QTc essentially unchanged (about 420-465 ms then).

Sinus rhythm 62 bpm, PR about 170 ms, QRS 98 ms, prominent left-sided voltage (V5 R 2.7 mV), frontal axis about +65 degrees. Grossly prolonged repolarisation with T peak near 400 ms and T end near 485 ms: QT 534 ms at RR 0.97 s, QTc (Bazett) 543 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 was sinus bradycardia 53 bpm with QTc 438 ms, so QTc has increased by about 105 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 103 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.39-1.07 s, CV 0.28) with no reproducible P wave before any QRS (beat-to-beat P-window correlation only 0.38), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 80 ms; net QRS negative in II, III and aVF with positive I/aVL gives a left axis of about -58 degrees. QT 310 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 403 ms. Only ECG on file.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 6/17/2026 to 1/6/2027). Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 6/17/2026) are acceptable. Also on metoprolol succinate; marked QTc prolongation on amiodarone in a 95-year-old requires prescriber review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo window of 30 days applies: ECG due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025, when it first appears in the current medication list. ECG 106885519 was obtained 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 543 ms - see the separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026; it is absent from the 2/18/2026 medication list and present from 8/1/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. The only ECG on file (106035722) is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was first ordered at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so the revised 14-day window applies and an ECG was due by 4/24/2026. The only ECG (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - inside the superseded 30-day window but outside the 14-day requirement - so the requirement was not met in time and remains overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracing 3/9/2025), but the due date falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation time, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026; start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG exists in the chart for this patient, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - with the report requested by fax and not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined from the chart.

Cardiology clinic clinician note of 9/1/2026 documents a warfarin dose change (INR 1.6 subtherapeutic, increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily, recheck INR). Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR(PT) 2.3 was drawn 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

Anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 documents a warfarin dose change made under the clinic protocol (home INR 3.4; warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily), which the 6/1/2024 standing order permits pharmacists to make. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR(PT) in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, and the reported home INR was the pre-change value. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 10:55 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72." Both ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at about 140-145 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, contradicting the documented sinus rhythm at rate 72.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current prescription (ordered 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027) despite outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 documenting admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The clinic reissued apixaban without documenting that review; concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel further increase bleeding risk. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, combined systolic/diastolic CHF), hypertension, age 80 (2), diabetes mellitus type 2, prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual deficits (2), vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis), female sex. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only; no oral anticoagulant is prescribed. Guideline-recommended (Class 1) anticoagulation is absent - antiplatelet therapy alone is not an acceptable substitute.

71-year-old woman with charted paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0). CHA2DS2-VASc 5: hypertension, age 71 (65-74), prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia/hemiparesis (2 points), female sex. Current medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate; no anticoagulant is prescribed at any clinic visit through 6/23/2026. Rate control only, without guideline-recommended (Class 1) oral anticoagulation, in a patient with prior stroke.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation charted as a condition and carried in the history of every cardiology clinic note (10/10/2025 to 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3: hypertension, age 71 (65-74), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). Only current medication is levothyroxine 50 mcg daily; no oral anticoagulant and no antiplatelet. Score of 3 in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of any anticoagulant needs review (past procedural haemorrhage is noted in the history and should be weighed).

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 7/18/2026 to 12/26/2026). Most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm 68 bpm with QT 492 ms and RR 0.88 s, giving a Bazett QTc of about 525 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Latest electrolytes 3/18/2026: potassium 3.8 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both low-normal). Note of 5/14/2024 recorded this ECG as having an acceptable QT, which the measured interval does not support.

Taking citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 7/15/2026 to 1/7/2027; 40 mg exceeds the 20 mg maximum usually advised on QT grounds). Most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm 70 bpm with QT 487 ms and RR 0.86 s, Bazett QTc about 526 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 7/12/2026 to 1/9/2027, started at the 11/10/2025 cardiology clinic visit). Most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm 62 bpm with QT 534 ms and RR 0.97 s, Bazett QTc about 543 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 6/9/2026) are normal. QTc rose from 438 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing after amiodarone was started.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with mild variability; upright P in II/aVF, one P per QRS, PR 122 ms. Narrow QRS 80 ms with normal precordial progression, frontal axis about +48 degrees. QT 324 ms at RR 0.74 s gives QTc 376 ms. No conduction block. No prior tracing for comparison. Confirms the 3/7/2026 note documenting sinus rhythm and satisfies the post-citalopram ECG requirement.

Sinus tachycardia 104 bpm, regular, discrete upright P in II with PR about 130 ms. QRS 94 ms, axis about +40 degrees, tall upright T in V2-V3. QT 337 ms at RR 0.58 s, QTc 443 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG 6/20/2025 was sinus tachycardia 147 bpm with PR about 125 ms and QTc about 400-420 ms; rate has slowed, with no new arrhythmia and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus tachycardia about 109 bpm, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II and PR about 120 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis about +36 degrees. QT 330 ms at RR 0.55 s, QTc (Bazett) 445 ms - upper normal. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG on file, so no comparison available.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean ventricular rate about 136 bpm (peak instantaneous rate near 170). RR intervals vary chaotically from 0.35 to 0.65 s with no consistent atrial activity preceding the QRS complexes, so PR is not measurable. QRS 100 ms, frontal axis near 0 degrees. QT 296 ms at mean RR 0.44 s, QTc (Bazett) about 458 ms (rate-correction unreliable at this rate). The tracing 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094) was also atrial fibrillation at about 134-142 bpm with QTc 453 ms, so there is no change between the two. Both contradict the same-day note of sinus rhythm at 72 bpm.

Regular supraventricular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s) with consistent low-amplitude atrial deflections about 150 ms before each QRS; P vector is leftward/superior (positive in I, low-amplitude negative in II/aVF), so a low atrial pacemaker cannot be excluded, but the rhythm is regular and one-to-one and is read as sinus. QRS 86 ms, tall R in I/aVL with net negative II/III, frontal axis about -25 degrees. QTc 431 ms. Prior ECG 4/27/2025 showed the same pattern at 60 bpm with QTc 404 ms - no new arrhythmia, block, or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular, with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 118 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +5 degrees. QT 292 ms at RR 0.62 s, QTc 373 ms. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG on file for this patient.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s, CV 0.005), upright P waves in II with PR about 195 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 86 ms, axis about +49 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 388 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus 108 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QTc 411 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no bundle branch block and QTc change of only -23 ms.

Sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis about +45 degrees. Markedly prolonged repolarisation: T wave peaks near 370 ms and ends near 455 ms after the R wave, QT 492 ms at RR 0.88 s, QTc (Bazett) 525 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 11/23/2022 was sinus 74 bpm with QTc 362 ms, so QTc has increased by roughly 160 ms - relevant to ongoing escitalopram (see QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia 121 bpm, strikingly regular (RR 0.497 s). Upright P in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR about 150 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, tall R in V5/V6 with rS in V1-V2, frontal axis about +67 degrees. QT 280 ms at RR 0.50 s, QTc 397 ms. No conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, so no comparison possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, axis about +58 degrees, QT 325 ms at RR 0.59 s giving QTc 423 ms. No conduction block. The immediately preceding tracing (102910502, obtained 34 seconds earlier the same morning) was identical - sinus 100 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc 422 ms - so there are no interval or rhythm changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with low-amplitude but consistent P waves in II and PR about 168 ms; no dropped beats or Wenckebach on this 10-second sample despite the charted history of Mobitz II block. QRS 92 ms, axis about +35 degrees, QTc 401 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 was sinus 58 bpm with one ectopic beat, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms - no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia 122 bpm (RR 0.494 s, very regular), P waves upright in II with PR about 150 ms. QRS is now narrow at about 76 ms with low limb-lead voltage; net QRS is negative in I and positive in III/aVF, giving a rightward frontal axis (about +110 to +140 degrees). QTc roughly 418 ms. On the tracing 13 hours earlier (106516875, same day 01:33) QRS was 130-155 ms with an rSR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - typical right bundle branch block - which has now resolved, indicating intermittent RBBB. QTc essentially unchanged (about 420-465 ms then).

Sinus rhythm 62 bpm, PR about 170 ms, QRS 98 ms, prominent left-sided voltage (V5 R 2.7 mV), frontal axis about +65 degrees. Grossly prolonged repolarisation with T peak near 400 ms and T end near 485 ms: QT 534 ms at RR 0.97 s, QTc (Bazett) 543 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 was sinus bradycardia 53 bpm with QTc 438 ms, so QTc has increased by about 105 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 103 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.39-1.07 s, CV 0.28) with no reproducible P wave before any QRS (beat-to-beat P-window correlation only 0.38), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 80 ms; net QRS negative in II, III and aVF with positive I/aVL gives a left axis of about -58 degrees. QT 310 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 403 ms. Only ECG on file.

Regular supraventricular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s) with consistent low-amplitude atrial deflections about 150 ms before each QRS; P vector is leftward/superior (positive in I, low-amplitude negative in II/aVF), so a low atrial pacemaker cannot be excluded, but the rhythm is regular and one-to-one and is read as sinus. QRS 86 ms, tall R in I/aVL with net negative II/III, frontal axis about -25 degrees. QTc 431 ms. Prior ECG 4/27/2025 showed the same pattern at 60 bpm with QTc 404 ms - no new arrhythmia, block, or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate about 63 bpm. Confirms the 3/7/2026 note documenting sinus rhythm and satisfies the post-citalopram ECG requirement.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean ventricular rate about 136 bpm (peak instantaneous rate near 170). RR intervals vary chaotically from 0.35 to 0.65 s with no consistent atrial activity preceding the QRS complexes, so PR is not measurable. QRS 100 ms, frontal axis near 0 degrees. QT 296 ms at mean RR 0.44 s, QTc (Bazett) about 458 ms (rate-correction unreliable at this rate). The tracing 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094) was also atrial fibrillation at about 134-142 bpm with QTc 453 ms, so there is no change between the two. Both contradict the same-day note of sinus rhythm at 72 bpm.

Regular supraventricular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s) with consistent low-amplitude atrial deflections about 150 ms before each QRS; P vector is leftward/superior (positive in I, low-amplitude negative in II/aVF), so a low atrial pacemaker cannot be excluded, but the rhythm is regular and one-to-one and is read as sinus. QRS 86 ms, tall R in I/aVL with net negative II/III, frontal axis about -25 degrees. QTc 431 ms. Prior ECG 4/27/2025 showed the same pattern at 60 bpm with QTc 404 ms - no new arrhythmia, block, or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular, with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 118 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +5 degrees. QT 292 ms at RR 0.62 s, QTc 373 ms. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG on file for this patient.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 0.83 s), upright P in II with PR about 140 ms. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +21 degrees. QT 373 ms, QTc (Bazett) 409 ms. Atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate about 63 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.70, 0.74, 1.13, 1.15, 1.16 s; CV 0.21) with no organised P wave in any lead before the QRS complexes, so PR is not measurable. QRS 92 ms, frontal axis about +14 degrees. QT approximately 430 ms at mean RR 0.96 s, QTc (Bazett) about 440 ms. Sinus rhythm/borderline sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with clear upright P waves in II (0.2 mV) and PR about 115 ms. QRS 88 ms, tall R in II/aVF, frontal axis about +62 degrees. Baseline tracing predates the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, very regular (RR 0.72 s), upright P in II/aVF with PR about 142 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees. QT 342 ms, QTc (Bazett) 403 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 0.78 s), with prominent upright P waves in II/aVF (0.26 mV) and PR about 160-165 ms. Narrow QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +63 degrees. Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s, CV 0.005), upright P waves in II with PR about 195 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 86 ms, axis about +49 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 388 ms. Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean ventricular rate about 147 bpm. Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with low-amplitude but consistent P waves in II and PR about 168 ms; no dropped beats or Wenckebach on this 10-second sample despite the charted history of Mobitz II block. QRS 92 ms, axis about +35 degrees, QTc 401 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 was sinus 58 bpm with one ectopic beat, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms - no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia 122 bpm (RR 0.494 s, very regular), P waves upright in II with PR about 150 ms. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 was sinus bradycardia 53 bpm with QTc 438 ms, so QTc has increased by about 105 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 103 bpm. interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with mild variability; upright P in II/aVF, one P per QRS, PR 122 ms. Narrow QRS 80 ms with normal precordial progression, frontal axis about +48 degrees. QT 324 ms at RR 0.74 s gives QTc 376 ms. No conduction block. No prior tracing for comparison. Confirms the 3/7/2026 note documenting sinus rhythm and satisfies the post-citalopram ECG requirement.

Sinus tachycardia 104 bpm, regular, discrete upright P in II with PR about 130 ms. QRS 94 ms, axis about +40 degrees, tall upright T in V2-V3. QT 337 ms at RR 0.58 s, QTc 443 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG 6/20/2025 was sinus tachycardia 147 bpm with PR about 125 ms and QTc about 400-420 ms; rate has slowed, with no new arrhythmia and no QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus tachycardia about 109 bpm, essentially regular, with upright P waves in II and PR about 120 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis about +36 degrees. QT 330 ms at RR 0.55 s, QTc (Bazett) 445 ms - upper normal. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG on file, so no comparison available.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean ventricular rate about 136 bpm (peak instantaneous rate near 170). RR intervals vary chaotically from 0.35 to 0.65 s with no consistent atrial activity preceding the QRS complexes, so PR is not measurable. QRS 100 ms, frontal axis near 0 degrees. QT 296 ms at mean RR 0.44 s, QTc (Bazett) about 458 ms (rate-correction unreliable at this rate). The tracing 2 hours 23 minutes earlier the same evening (107914094) was also atrial fibrillation at about 134-142 bpm with QTc 453 ms, so there is no change between the two. Both contradict the same-day note of sinus rhythm at 72 bpm.

Regular supraventricular rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 0.87 s) with consistent low-amplitude atrial deflections about 150 ms before each QRS; P vector is leftward/superior (positive in I, low-amplitude negative in II/aVF), so a low atrial pacemaker cannot be excluded, but the rhythm is regular and one-to-one and is read as sinus. QRS 86 ms, tall R in I/aVL with net negative II/III, frontal axis about -25 degrees. QTc 431 ms. Prior ECG 4/27/2025 showed the same pattern at 60 bpm with QTc 404 ms - no new arrhythmia, block, or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular, with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 118 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +5 degrees. QT 292 ms at RR 0.62 s, QTc 373 ms. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG on file for this patient.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 0.83 s), upright P in II with PR about 140 ms. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +21 degrees. QT 373 ms, QTc (Bazett) 409 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG on file; it predates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start, so it does not satisfy the post-start ECG requirement.

Atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate about 63 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.70, 0.74, 1.13, 1.15, 1.16 s; CV 0.21) with no organised P wave in any lead before the QRS complexes, so PR is not measurable. QRS 92 ms, frontal axis about +14 degrees. QT approximately 430 ms at mean RR 0.96 s, QTc (Bazett) about 440 ms. Prior ECG three days earlier (11/12/2024) was normal sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with PR 162 ms and QTc 396 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation; the QTc difference (about 45 ms) does not reach 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm/borderline sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with clear upright P waves in II (0.2 mV) and PR about 115 ms. QRS 88 ms, tall R in II/aVF, frontal axis about +62 degrees. QT 422 ms at RR 1.03 s, QTc 416 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG the previous day (3/8/2025) was sinus 62 bpm, QRS 88 ms, QTc 436 ms - no change. Baseline tracing predates the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start.

Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, very regular (RR 0.72 s), upright P in II/aVF with PR about 142 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees. QT 342 ms, QTc (Bazett) 403 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG on file.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 0.78 s), with prominent upright P waves in II/aVF (0.26 mV) and PR about 160-165 ms. Narrow QRS 70 ms, frontal axis about +63 degrees. Broad symmetric T waves; QT approximately 405-430 ms at RR 0.78 s, giving QTc (Bazett) of roughly 470 ms - borderline prolonged but below 500 ms. No conduction block. Prior ECG 2/2/2020 was sinus 75 bpm with QTc about 495 ms, so the change is well under 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s, CV 0.005), upright P waves in II with PR about 195 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 86 ms, axis about +49 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 388 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus 108 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QTc 411 ms) there is no new arrhythmia, no bundle branch block and QTc change of only -23 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with prolonged AV conduction: P onset about 250 ms and QRS onset about 40 ms before the R peak, PR approximately 205-210 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 82 ms with dominant R in V4-V6, frontal axis about +12 degrees. QT 395 ms at RR 1.10 s, QTc (Bazett) 376 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 11/30/2024 was sinus 51 bpm with a single ectopic beat, PR about 180-185 ms and QTc 360 ms; no new arrhythmia, bundle branch block or 60 ms QTc shift.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean ventricular rate about 147 bpm. RR intervals range from 0.31 to 0.60 s with no repeatable atrial deflection before the QRS (P-window correlation 0.15), so PR is not measurable. QRS about 80 ms, frontal axis near -8 degrees. QT 261 ms at mean RR 0.41 s, QTc (Bazett) about 410 ms. The tracing 12 hours earlier (9/12/2025 18:57) was sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with PR 144 ms and QTc 405 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation; intravenous amiodarone was started the same morning.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm with upright P waves in II (0.22 mV) and PR about 165 ms, confirming the same-day note of sinus rhythm. QRS 92 ms, frontal axis about +12 degrees. QT 355 ms at RR 0.82 s, QTc (Bazett) 392 ms. No conduction block. The prior tracing of 11/21/2025 was sinus 67 bpm with a markedly long QT (about 500 ms, QTc 529 ms); repolarisation has now normalised, a QTc decrease of well over 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm (RR 0.81 s) after two early supraventricular beats at the start of the recording; thereafter the rhythm is regular with consistent upright P waves in II and PR about 175 ms. QRS 90 ms, frontal axis about +57 degrees. QT 382 ms, QTc (Bazett) 425 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, very regular (RR 0.538 s, CV 0.003), with a single upright P wave in II about 145 ms before each QRS - no flutter waves and no second atrial deflection per cycle, so the charted atrial flutter is not present on this tracing. QRS 96 ms with deep S in V1 and tall R in II, frontal axis about +35 degrees. QT 295 ms, QTc (Bazett) 402 ms. Prior ECG 7/4/2022 was virtually identical (sinus 115 bpm, QRS 96 ms, QTc 397 ms) - no change.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm interrupted by one early beat with a compensatory pause (RR 0.55 s then 1.36 s); otherwise regular at RR 0.98 s with broad low-amplitude P waves and PR about 195-200 ms (borderline, just short of first-degree block). QRS 104 ms, dominant R in I/aVL with net negative II, III and aVF, giving a left axis of about -30 to -35 degrees (left anterior fascicular pattern). QT 377 ms, QTc (Bazett) 381 ms. No bundle branch block. Single ECG on file - no atrial fibrillation captured despite the charted paroxysmal AF.

Regular rhythm at 69 bpm with one atrial deflection before every QRS at a constant interval of about 140 ms, read as sinus. The limb leads are globally inverted - QRS and P both negative in I, II and aVL and positive in aVR - while precordial progression is normal, giving a calculated frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme/north-west quadrant); left-right arm lead reversal should be excluded before accepting this axis as real. QRS 90 ms, QT 349 ms, QTc (Bazett) 376 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Only ECG on file; it postdates the 4/10/2026 escitalopram start by 19 days.

Sinus rhythm 68 bpm, PR 124 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis about +45 degrees. Markedly prolonged repolarisation: T wave peaks near 370 ms and ends near 455 ms after the R wave, QT 492 ms at RR 0.88 s, QTc (Bazett) 525 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 11/23/2022 was sinus 74 bpm with QTc 362 ms, so QTc has increased by roughly 160 ms - relevant to ongoing escitalopram (see QT safety item).

Sinus tachycardia 121 bpm, strikingly regular (RR 0.497 s). Upright P in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR about 150 ms. Narrow QRS 72 ms, tall R in V5/V6 with rS in V1-V2, frontal axis about +67 degrees. QT 280 ms at RR 0.50 s, QTc 397 ms. No conduction abnormality. Single ECG on file, so no comparison possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, PR 144 ms, QRS 88 ms, axis about +58 degrees, QT 325 ms at RR 0.59 s giving QTc 423 ms. No conduction block. The immediately preceding tracing (102910502, obtained 34 seconds earlier the same morning) was identical - sinus 100 bpm, QRS 90 ms, QTc 422 ms - so there are no interval or rhythm changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with low-amplitude but consistent P waves in II and PR about 168 ms; no dropped beats or Wenckebach on this 10-second sample despite the charted history of Mobitz II block. QRS 92 ms, axis about +35 degrees, QTc 401 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 was sinus 58 bpm with one ectopic beat, QRS 88 ms, QTc 392 ms - no significant change.

Sinus tachycardia 122 bpm (RR 0.494 s, very regular), P waves upright in II with PR about 150 ms. QRS is now narrow at about 76 ms with low limb-lead voltage; net QRS is negative in I and positive in III/aVF, giving a rightward frontal axis (about +110 to +140 degrees). QTc roughly 418 ms. On the tracing 13 hours earlier (106516875, same day 01:33) QRS was 130-155 ms with an rSR' in V1 and wide terminal S waves in I and V6 - typical right bundle branch block - which has now resolved, indicating intermittent RBBB. QTc essentially unchanged (about 420-465 ms then).

Sinus rhythm 62 bpm, PR about 170 ms, QRS 98 ms, prominent left-sided voltage (V5 R 2.7 mV), frontal axis about +65 degrees. Grossly prolonged repolarisation with T peak near 400 ms and T end near 485 ms: QT 534 ms at RR 0.97 s, QTc (Bazett) 543 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 was sinus bradycardia 53 bpm with QTc 438 ms, so QTc has increased by about 105 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 103 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.39-1.07 s, CV 0.28) with no reproducible P wave before any QRS (beat-to-beat P-window correlation only 0.38), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 80 ms; net QRS negative in II, III and aVF with positive I/aVL gives a left axis of about -58 degrees. QT 310 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 403 ms. Only ECG on file.

Prior ECG 4/27/2025 showed the same pattern at 60 bpm with QTc 404 ms - no new arrhythmia, block, or QTc change of 60 ms or more.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular, with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 118 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +5 degrees. QT 292 ms at RR 0.62 s, QTc 373 ms. No conduction abnormality. Only ECG on file for this patient.

Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 0.83 s), upright P in II with PR about 140 ms. QRS 82 ms, frontal axis about +21 degrees. QT 373 ms, QTc (Bazett) 409 ms. Atrial fibrillation, mean ventricular rate about 63 bpm. Normal sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, very regular (RR 0.72 s), upright P in II/aVF with PR about 142 ms. Narrow QRS 74 ms, frontal axis about +53 degrees. QT 342 ms, QTc (Bazett) 403 ms. No bundle branch block or AV block. Single ECG on file.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular (RR 0.50 s, CV 0.005), upright P waves in II with PR about 195 ms (upper normal, not first-degree block). QRS 86 ms, axis about +49 degrees. QTc (Bazett) 388 ms. Grossly prolonged repolarisation with T peak near 400 ms and T end near 485 ms: QT 534 ms at RR 0.97 s, QTc (Bazett) 543 ms. No bundle branch block. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 was sinus bradycardia 53 bpm with QTc 438 ms, so QTc has increased by about 105 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 103 bpm. RR intervals are irregularly irregular (0.39-1.07 s, CV 0.28) with no reproducible P wave before any QRS (beat-to-beat P-window correlation only 0.38), so no PR interval is measurable. QRS 80 ms; net QRS negative in II, III and aVF with positive I/aVL gives a left axis of about -58 degrees. QT 310 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 403 ms. Only ECG on file.

The 7/15/2026 cardiology note documents a switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage and starts apixaban, but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped, so the patient is on two DOACs simultaneously.

Taking amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 6/17/2026 to 1/6/2027). Most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm about 59 bpm with QT 564 ms and RR 1.01 s, Bazett QTc about 561 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo. Most recent potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 6/17/2026) are acceptable. Also on metoprolol succinate; marked QTc prolongation on amiodarone in a 95-year-old requires prescriber review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start is on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was obtained 3/7/2026, five days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo window of 30 days applies: ECG due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was obtained 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 11/10/2025, when it first appears in the current medication list. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo window of 30 days applies: ECG due by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was obtained 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 543 ms - see the separate QT safety item).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/1/2026; it is absent from the 2/18/2026 medication list and present from 8/1/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. The only ECG on file (106035722) is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was first ordered at the cardiology clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so the revised 14-day window applies and an ECG was due by 4/24/2026. The only ECG (107859369) was recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start - inside the superseded 30-day window but outside the 14-day requirement - so the requirement was not met in time and remains overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracing 3/9/2025), but the due date falls after the 9/24/2026 evaluation time, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 8/10/2026; start on or after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG exists in the chart for this patient, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - with the report requested by fax and not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined from the chart.

Cardiology clinic clinician note of 9/1/2026 documents a warfarin dose change (INR 1.6 subtherapeutic, increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily, recheck INR). Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR is required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. INR(PT) 2.3 was drawn 9/5/2026, four days after the change, so the requirement was met.

Anticoagulation clinic pharmacist note of 9/10/2026 documents a warfarin dose change made under the clinic protocol (home INR 3.4; warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily), which the 6/1/2024 standing order permits pharmacists to make. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR(PT) in the chart is 2.7 from 6/17/2026; no INR has been drawn since the dose change, and the reported home INR was the pre-change value. Overdue as of 9/24/2026.

Cardiology clinic note of 6/10/2026 10:55 states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72." Both ECGs recorded the same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at about 140-145 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, contradicting the documented sinus rhythm at rate 72.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains a current prescription (ordered 8/20/2026, valid to 1/4/2027) despite outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 documenting admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper gastrointestinal bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The clinic reissued apixaban without documenting that review; concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel further increase bleeding risk. Anticoagulation should not continue without prescriber review.

80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note from 9/12/2025 through 6/22/2026. CHA2DS2-VASc 9: congestive heart failure (hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, combined systolic/diastolic CHF), hypertension, age 80 (2), diabetes mellitus type 2, prior cerebral infarction/TIA with residual deficits (2), vascular disease (old myocardial infarction, coronary atherosclerosis), female sex. Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and gabapentin only; no oral anticoagulant is prescribed. Guideline-recommended (Class 1) anticoagulation is absent - antiplatelet therapy alone is not an acceptable substitute.

71-year-old woman with charted paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (I48.0). CHA2DS2-VASc 5: hypertension, age 71 (65-74), prior cerebral infarction with residual hemiplegia/hemiparesis (2 points), female sex. Current medications are famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate; no anticoagulant is prescribed at any clinic visit through 6/23/2026. Rate control only, without guideline-recommended (Class 1) oral anticoagulation, in a patient with prior stroke.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation charted as a condition and carried in the history of every cardiology clinic note (10/10/2025 to 6/27/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 3: hypertension, age 71 (65-74), vascular disease (coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery). Only current medication is levothyroxine 50 mcg daily; no oral anticoagulant and no antiplatelet. Score of 3 in a man meets the Class 1 recommendation for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of any anticoagulant needs review (past procedural haemorrhage is noted in the history and should be weighed).

Taking escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug (current prescription 7/18/2026 to 12/26/2026). Most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm 68 bpm with QT 492 ms and RR 0.88 s, giving a Bazett QTc of about 525 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Latest electrolytes 3/18/2026: potassium 3.8 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both low-normal). Note of 5/14/2024 recorded this ECG as having an acceptable QT, which the measured interval does not support.

Most recent potassium 4.6 mEq/L (7/15/2026) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (3/8/2025) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes.

Most recent potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 6/9/2026) are normal. QTc rose from 438 ms on the 6/7/2025 tracing after amiodarone was started.
